text:
maria: Heads-up — just hit a weird state in the deploy queue during this morning's rollout window. two canaries got scheduled to start overlapping the change window boundary and deploy-bot queued them concurrently so approvals interleaved.

aj: ugh. can you paste the deploy-bot log lines?

maria: sure — snippet below. seems like the canary start times crossed the changewindow cutoff and the approval queue didn't enforce per-window ordering.

maria: ```
2026-04-01T09:58:12Z deploy-bot INFO enqueue canary: rollout_id=rl-2026-04-01-93 window=2026-04-01T10:00:00Z-2026-04-01T11:00:00Z approvers=[chloe,aj]
2026-04-01T09:59:03Z deploy-bot INFO enqueue canary: rollout_id=rl-2026-04-01-94 window=2026-04-01T10:30:00Z-2026-04-01T11:30:00Z approvers=[devin,chloe]
2026-04-01T10:00:01Z deploy-bot INFO start approval for rl-2026-04-01-93 assigned=chloe
2026-04-01T10:30:02Z deploy-bot INFO start approval for rl-2026-04-01-94 assigned=devin
2026-04-01T10:45:10Z deploy-bot WARN approval conflict: approver=chloe vote=approve on rl-93 then vote=approve on rl-94 within same changewindow
```

devin: so chloe got pinged for both and approved both. the problem is the second canary's traffic split started partially inside the first canary's window, causing our telemetry to mix. we ended up with blended metrics for the first 15m.

chloe: sorry — will avoid approving overlapping ones when possible. but the UX made it unclear they overlapped; approvals came from different threads.

maria: no blame — this is a platform issue. we need either (A) deploy-bot to enforce non-overlapping approvals per approver within a change window, or (B) UI highlight when a requested approval will cause a metrics overlap, or (C) auto-serialize canaries that share any time range.

aj: +1 on (C) as a safe default, but we should add an escape hatch. proposal: default to serialize if windows overlap > 0s, but allow an explicit `concurrent_ok=true` flag in the rollout spec to opt-in.

devin: also want telemetry guard — if two canaries overlap, route a separate telemetry namespace so dashboards show separate buckets even if traffic overlaps. that way we at least avoid mixing.

maria: good point. short-term: can we push a quick change to deploy-bot so it rejects new approval starts that would cause an approver to have >1 active approval in the same window? that should be small (queue check + error).

aj: should be doable. i can put up a PR to the auth/assign flow. will add a guard that returns 409 with message `approver-busy-withing-window` and include the other rollout id.

chloe: will that surface in the console? right now it just shows a generic "approval failed" toast. we need a clearer modal explaining overlap and showing the other rollout time ranges.

maria: yes — devex can do a tiny UX change to map that 409 -> modal with both windows and "serialize / override" buttons. default UX should nudge to serialize.

devin: longer-term: (1) implement serialized default + opt-in concurrent flag, (2) telemetry namespace separation, (3) console timeline visuals for overlapping rollouts.

aj: i'll prototype the backend guard tonight. maria — do you want to own the console modal copy?

maria: happy to. i'll draft copy and add a small CTA for "Request concurrent approval" which will create a dedicated override ticket that SRE can audit.

sre-alerts: FYI — when metrics are blended the canary detection SLOs misfire and we could auto-roll back mistakenly. let's add a temporary mitigation: if overlapping canaries are detected, disable automatic rollback until we reconcile telemetry.

devin: agree. add flag `suppress-autorollback-on-overlap=true` to the rollout defaults for now.

aj: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/deploy-bot/pull/1981 — implements approver-busy guard + 409 payload. added unit tests.

maria: thanks. i'll add console copy and chloe can review. can we ship the guard as a hotfix before next weekday rollout?

aj: aiming for the next patch deploy window at 2026-04-02T03:00Z. it should be low-risk.

chloe: will review copy and coordinate. if the guard blocks legit parallel runs we can use the override ticket flow to unblock temporarily. :thumbsup:

maria: great. follow-ups: aj -> backend guard rollout, devex -> modal copy, devops -> ensure patch window includes the change, devops/sre -> add suppress-autorollback flag. we'll reconvene after PR merges.

aj: noted. will post a short changelog when merged.

maria: thanks everyone — saved us from a noisy false-positive tomorrow.

(automated) deploy-bot: note: queued patch deploy for deploy-bot at 2026-04-02T03:00:00Z with tag=hotfix/approval-guard
